title: Kin Kin

bikeon.heading: Kin Kin
paras: Kin Kin's name has long been debated. The Queensland Government records it as reportedly coming from a Kabi word, kauin kauin, indicating the red soil drained by Kin Kin Creek, while many locals prefer "plenty of black ants", a story you'll see in the ant sculpture outside the general store. Timber getters worked the ranges from the late 1870s, floating logs down Kin Kin Creek to the sawmill on Lake Cootharaba. In 1905 the Lands Department opened 6,000 acres here for selection, and bananas and dairy followed; the Kin Kin Dairy Company ran from 1914 to 1937. The two storey hotel, designed by Cooroy architect William Fenwick, opened in November 1915. It lost its roof and verandahs in the 1971 tornado, took about three metres of floodwater in April 2009, and reopened in late 2023 after a long restoration. Main Street also keeps the old post office, bank and School of Arts.
